title: Scoped authorization topology and temporary elevation protocol
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Design a composable, deterministic role model and evaluation protocol for RBAC v2 that supports hierarchical resources, scope-limited roles, attribute-based constraints, and a Just-In-Time (JIT) temporary elevation (breakglass) flow tied to audit events and SAML attribute mappings. Goals: produce a clear permission matrix format, a resolution algorithm for conflicting grants/denies, an auditable temporary elevation protocol, and concrete migration guidance for existing rolesets. This ticket captures design decisions, acceptance criteria, and next engineering tasks.

Context and motivation: Current RBAC implementation is flat and does not express resource-scoped roles (e.g., dataset-reader at project vs cluster level), nor does it provide an auditable, time-limited elevation path for admin operations. Customers (enterprise, regulated) require: 1) fine-grained scope boundaries, 2) JIT elevation with approval or automated justification, 3) SAML attribute-driven role assertions, and 4) strong audit trails tying elevated tokens to an initiating actor and approval reason.

High-level requirements: 1) Role model must express: allowed actions, resource specificity, conditional constraints (time, IP, MFA), and precedence. 2) Evaluation must be O(log N) for deep hierarchies and deterministic across runtime modes (hosted, dedicated, private). 3) Temporary elevation tokens must be short lived, auditable, able to be revoked, and correlate to the original requestor and approval chain. 4) Audit logs must capture before/after role state, request payload, SAML attributes used for mapping, and token identifiers. 5) Migration must provide compatibility shims for existing role bindings and a rollout that avoids downtime for policy evaluation.

Out of scope: full attribute-based access control (ABAC) policy language, policy UI polish (handled by console team), and RBAC enforcement libraries for third-party customers (future follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable permission matrix format (CSV/JSON schema) that encodes role -> action -> resource-pattern -> constraint and precedence rules is approved by security review.
An algorithm doc describing how to resolve multiple bindings (grant vs deny vs conditional) with concrete examples across nested resources (tenant -> project -> bucket) is finalized.
Temporary elevation protocol defined: request flow, approval modes (auto, manual), token lifecycle (issued_at, expires_at, revoked flag), and audit entries schema accepted by compliance.
SAML mapping spec that demonstrates mapping SAML attributes (group, role, entitlements) to scoped roles and how assertion-based expiry is reconciled with the JIT token expiry.
Migration plan that includes a compatibility shim, data migration script outline, and a phased rollout checklist to avoid service interruption.
End-to-end test plan and QA checklist exist and include integration tests that simulate conflict resolution, elevation approval, and audit trail verification.
implementation_notes: Role representation: canonical JSON entries with fields: id, name, actions[], resource_selector (glob or path template), constraints{}, precedence_score (integer).

Evaluation engine: build a two-phase evaluator: 1) collect applicable bindings for resource lineage, 2) apply precedence rules (deny > grant unless higher precedence grant present) with short-circuiting for explicit denies.

Temporary elevation: mint a signed short-lived token (JWT v2) containing original_principal, elevation_reason_id, approved_by, approval_mode. Tokens minted by auth-service and checked by runtime with revocation list (in-memory cache + persisted revocations for audit).

SAML: add attribute mapping layer in identity service. Support attribute-to-role mapping time-based assertions. For on-prem, accept SAML mapping config via customer-managed YAML stored in KMS-encrypted config store.

Audit: new audit entries will include fields: event_type, principal, original_principal, role_binding_delta, resource_path, request_id, saml_attributes (masked where sensitive), token_id, approval_chain_ids. Ensure entries are immutable and forwarded to central logging and the console audit viewer.

Performance: resolver must use precomputed binding indices per resource shard and a small LRU cache keyed by (principal, resource_path, effective_action, cache_ttl) to meet 1ms median policy decision for hot paths.

Backward compatibility: implement 'roleset-compat' adapter in policy-loader that converts old flat bindings into scoped role bindings with best-effort resource selectors; log migrated mappings for operator review.
comments: 2026-02-27 Liam Chen: Started spike on evaluation algorithm. Found pathological case with 6-level deep nesting and many wildcard bindings causing linear scan. Plan: add per-level index and early deny detection.
2026-03-02 Asha Patel: Security reviewed initial permission matrix draft. Requested explicit deny semantics and a 'managed_by' field to separate system roles vs customer roles.
2026-03-05 Jon Rivera (Design): Suggested we add a UI hint field for console to display scope breadcrumbs. Also flagged need for consistent human-readable names for temporary elevation events.
2026-03-09 QA: Added integration test spec for token revocation race where runtime receives request with token cancelled concurrently. Test should assert immediate denial after revocation.
2026-03-11 Compliance (Emma Novak): Approved audit schema pending PII masking rules; asked for retention window configuration on per-tenant basis.
2026-03-13 Liam Chen: Implementation prototype merged to branch rbac/v2-spike; awaiting PR review. Next: wire revocation cache and add SAML mapping translator.
migration_plan: Phase 1: compatibility adapter in policy-loader to translate legacy bindings into scoped role bindings and populate a review log; Phase 2: emit warnings to customers for ambiguous bindings during a 2-week window; Phase 3: rollout enforcement by default behind a feature flag; Phase 4: monitor audit logs and performance dashboards for 4 weeks before full cutover. Provide rollback path via feature flag and migration snapshot.
rollout_plan: 1) Developer preview in staging with opt-in config 'rbac_v2_enabled' for specific orgs. 2) Beta rollout to 10% of customers for two weeks to validate behavior and telemetry. 3) Gradual ramp to 50% while running compatibility-mode for remaining customers. 4) Full enforcement after compliance signoff and performance SLAs met. Coordinate with Console team for exposure of elevation requests and with Identity team to deploy SAML mapping config UI.
